names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 16 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Isaachie Persul din Meţovo».

The nominative the day page's own `/name/1095.html` link carries in its `title`, «Святитель Исаак Бет-Селевкийский (Персидский), епископ, сщмч.», with «Святитель» and the two trailing rank words left off — `bishop` and `hieromartyr` are now in this folder's `types` — and both place epithets kept, the parenthesis being the calendar's own and not part of the fold key (BRIEF-ADDENDUM §2). The day's own line declines the three together, «Мчч. Симеона , Исаака и Вахтисия (IV).» `fk.mjs` on this form returned NONE before the write.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Симеона , Исаака и Вахтисия (IV).»

attestations.note: The same reading as on `simeon-martyr-16-may`: saint.gr's «Άγιοι Ισαάκιος, Συμεών και Βαχθισόης» for 16 Μαΐου and this calendar's «Мчч. Симеона , Исаака и Вахтисия» for 18 мая are the same three men, and `bachthisoes` already names this folder as one of its two companions. **The Russian makes him a bishop and a hieromartyr, which no other book in this folder does**: its name page heads him «Святитель Исаак Бет-Селевкийский (Персидский), епископ, сщмч.» — the hierarch Isaac of Beth-Seleucia, the Persian, bishop, hieromartyr. `hieromartyr` and `bishop` were added to `types` on that authority and `office` was set to the bare `Bishop`, because BRIEF-ADDENDUM §4 records that a see-bearing office string costs four locale translations a reader may not invent; the see is in the life instead. **No `dates` object was written**: the folder had none, and the page's own day line says the fourth century where its notice says the third. **The two epithets do not agree either** — doxologia.ro called him the Persian of Metsovo, a town in Epirus, and this calendar gives him a Persian see; the display name was not changed and both readings are in the life. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 16 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Isaachie Persul din Meţovo»
